query: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa, but its high Mo content increases the electronegativity difference and is associated with reduced plasticity. What single intervention could improve its room-temperature compressive strength–plasticity balance without sacrificing its high strength? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, the operative mechanism, the predicted change in strength and plasticity relative to the equiatomic disordered-BCC alloy, the conditions and limits under which the effect should occur, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Partial substitution of Mo with V in the equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo alloy will reduce bond heterogeneities caused by high Mo electronegativity, thereby improving dislocation mobility and plasticity during room-temperature compression while maintaining its high compressive yield strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo disordered BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with a compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa and reduced plasticity due to high Mo content.
generation.intervention: Replace a portion (e.g., approximately 25% of the Mo content) with vanadium (V).
generation.conditions: Alloy processing and testing at room temperature under compressive loading; the base alloy composition is maintained except for V substituting a fraction of Mo; standard melting and casting conditions to ensure a disordered BCC phase.
generation.structural_mediator: Reduction in the electronegativity difference and local bond heterogeneities, leading to modified lattice distortions which favor improved dislocation slip behavior.
generation.mechanism: By substituting part of Mo with a low-electronegativity element like V, the alloy experiences diminished point-to-point bonding heterogeneity. This adjustment is expected to lower the lattice friction stress (Peierls barrier) and create a microstructure that supports enhanced dislocation mobility. The solid-solution strengthening contribution is preserved, allowing the alloy to maintain high yield strength while plastic strain capacity is improved.
generation.predicted_outcome: The V-substituted alloy is predicted to retain a compressive yield strength close to 1719 MPa while exhibiting enhanced plasticity (i.e., increased compressive strain before failure), thus improving the strength–plasticity balance relative to the original equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo alloy.
generation.baseline: The unmodified equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo alloy, which shows high compressive yield strength (1719 MPa) but limited plasticity due to a high Mo-induced electronegativity difference.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is expected only with moderate substitution levels (e.g., around 25% Mo replaced by V) at room temperature and in conditions that preserve the disordered BCC phase. Excessive V content might alter phase stability or reduce yield strength significantly.
generation.uncertainty: The exact quantitative improvement in plasticity and the potential minor changes to yield strength are uncertain. There is also uncertainty regarding the optimal substitution level and possible subtle effects on phase stability that could emerge under different processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of alloys: (i) the baseline equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo and (ii) a modified variant where approximately 25% of the Mo is replaced with V under identical processing conditions. Perform room-temperature compressive tests to obtain stress–strain curves and measure yield strength, plastic strain, and work-hardening rates. Additionally, conduct microstructural analysis using TEM to assess dislocation structures and any evidence of altered lattice distortions.
measurements: TEM analysis of dislocation substructures and lattice distortions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the V-substituted alloy exhibits a significant drop in compressive yield strength (greater than ~10% below the baseline) or does not show a measurable improvement in plastic strain or work-hardening behavior compared to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Equiatomic CoCrNi medium-entropy alloys exhibit superior strength and ductility. In this work, a non-equiatomic CoCrNi alloy with low stacking fault energy was designed, and different fractions of V were added to control the stacking fault energy and lattice distortion. Mechanical properties were evaluated by tensile tests, and deformation microstructures were characterized by transmission electron microscope (TEM). The main deformation mechanisms of CoCrNiV alloy with low V content are dislocation slip, stacking faults, and deformation-induced HCP phase transformation, while the dominant deformation patterns of CoCrNiV alloy with high V contents are dislocation slip and stacking faults. The yield strength increases dramatically when the V content is high, and the strain-hardening behavior changes non-monotonically with increasing the V content. V addition increases the stacking fault energy (SFE) and lattice distortion. The lower strain-hardening rate of 6V alloy than that of 2V alloy is dominated by the SFE. Among single-phase HEAs/MEAs, CoCrNi MEAs with single-phase FCC structure have extraordinary tensile properties and fracture toughness due to their low stacking fault energy (SFE) and high solid-solution strengthening effect [,,,]. Sohn et al. [] found that the yield strength (σY) of FCC VCoNi alloy reaches 1 GPa (d = 2.0 ± 1.5 μm) through high solid-solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening effects and that the nanoscale dislocation substructure gives the alloy excellent ductility and strain-hardening capability. Therefore, the solid-solution strengthening plays an important role in improving the yield strength of HEAs/MEAs and is associated with the following factors: the interaction energy between fluctuations in local solute concentration and dislocations [], the charge transfer of atomic size and electronic states [] and short-range ordering (SRO) or clustering (SRC) []. It was shown that the presence of large atomic volume misfit of V in CoCrNi alloys produced a high solid-solution strengthening effect, which increased the yield strength of FCC and body-centered cubic (BCC) HEAs [].

reading.lever: Partially substitute Mo with a low-electronegativity element (e.g., V) to diminish bond heterogeneities and improve dislocation mobility.
reading.why: V substitution in related HEAs has effectively balanced strength and ductility, making it a promising route for NbZrTiHfMo.
